chapters.title: The Patient Messenger
chapters.teaser: A clear night, and a sky that is not one picture but many departures.
chapters.recap: Light is introduced as a messenger whose delay turns time into distance. The guide sets out why small timing errors matter.

chapters.title: Clocks That Disagree
chapters.teaser: A workbench of clocks, each counting something that repeats.
chapters.recap: Every clock drifts, and orbiting clocks drift in a particular way. A single tuned number corrects them before launch.

chapters.title: Listening to the Edge of the Sky
chapters.teaser: Two dishes on two continents turn toward the same faint point.
chapters.recap: Radio dishes time a quasar's noise to measure the Earth itself, closing the loop back to the phone.

states.text: The guide's patient messenger, whose travel time becomes distance.
Who once judged distance by the gap between a flash and its boom.
The steadiest clock in the guide, counting an atom's flips.
A blazing distant galaxy core, fixed enough to measure against.

annotations.anchor: a few tens of microseconds a day
annotations.note: Speed slows an orbiting clock and weaker gravity speeds it up; for navigation satellites the second effect wins.
